characters.name: Alice
characters.description: About seven or eight; straight brown hair in a ribbon, knee‑length blue pinafore dress, white pinafore apron, sensible boots; curious expression, slim child proportions. Carries a small handkerchief and later a pocket with cake or bottle.

characters.name: White Rabbit
characters.description: Small white rabbit in a waistcoat and pocket watch; pink eyes, nervous posture, waistcoat slightly rumpled, brass watch on a chain. Always in motion, muttering about being late.

characters.name: Mouse
characters.description: A small brown mouse with bright anxious eyes and a sensible tail. Wears no clothing but has expressive eyebrows and habit of sitting upright to speak.

characters.name: Caterpillar
characters.description: A large blue caterpillar with a rounded segmented body, expressive sleepy eyes and a thoughtful, slightly stern face. Rests comfortably on top of a broad mushroom. Original watercolor design, with no smoking equipment.

characters.name: Duchess
characters.description: A stout, sharp‑faced woman in an oversized cap and patched dress; carries a baby. Her apron is floury and pepper‑sprinkled; moves with abrupt gestures and a rough voice.

characters.name: Cheshire Cat
characters.description: Striped feline with a perpetually wide grin and luminous eyes. Semi‑transparent at times, with long whiskers and a tail that curls like a painted ribbon; sits high in trees or on hearths.

characters.name: March Hare
characters.description: A wild‑eyed hare with messy fur, tea‑stained waistcoat and an always‑crumpled bow tie. Energetic, twitchy hands and frequently spilling teacups.

characters.name: Hatter
characters.description: A thin eccentric adult man with a tall plain brown top hat, curly auburn hair, green waistcoat, ochre jacket and mismatched socks. Lively eyebrows and a puzzled smile. No lettering on his hat.

characters.name: Dormouse
characters.description: Tiny, sleepy mouse who dozes between teacups. Wears a tiny waistcoat and speaks in soft, drowsy asides when roused.

characters.name: Mock Turtle
characters.description: A gentle imaginary creature with a turtle shell, a calf-like head, small hooves and large soulful eyes. Sad but friendly expression. Soft green shell and warm brown face, with no clothing or hat.

characters.name: Gryphon
characters.description: A heavy‑chested creature with an eagle's head and lion's body. Proud posture, shaggy mane, and clipped wings; wears a simple collar as if a court escort.

characters.name: Queen of Hearts
characters.description: A fierce woman in a red gown patterned with hearts, a small crown perched on swept hair. Short, commanding stature, flushed cheeks, and a dramatic, snapping voice.

source.name: Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland by Lewis Carroll (1865)

pages.title: Down the Rabbit Hole
pages.text: Alice was bored beside her sister when a white rabbit hurried past. It wore a waistcoat and carried a watch! Alice followed it down a hole and fell into a strange hall. A tiny door led to a lovely garden. But getting through it would not be easy.
pages.scene: Alice, a young girl with straight brown hair and a ribbon, kneels in a tall curious hall beside a very small door. A little gold key rests on a glass table. Through the doorway shines a beautiful garden. Original watercolor design, no readable lettering.
pages.sourceNote: Original narrative episode: Down the Rabbit Hole.
pages.alt: Alice, a young girl with straight brown hair and a ribbon, kneels in a tall curious hall beside a very small door. A little gold key rests on a glass table. Through the doorway shines a beautiful garden. Original watercolor design, no readable lettering.

pages.title: A Sea of Tears
pages.text: A strange drink made Alice small. A little cake made her huge! She cried until her tears formed a pool. Then a fan made her shrink again, and she fell into her own tears. Nearby, a mouse was swimming too. Wonderland was getting stranger every minute.
pages.scene: Tiny Alice and a small brown Mouse swim safely through a shallow magical pool inside the great hall. The legs of a glass table tower above them. Gentle ripples, curious expressions, playful scale, only one Alice at one size, no bottles or readable text.
pages.sourceNote: Original narrative episode: A Sea of Tears.
pages.alt: Tiny Alice and a small brown Mouse swim safely through a shallow magical pool inside the great hall. The legs of a glass table tower above them. Gentle ripples, curious expressions, playful scale, only one Alice at one size, no bottles or readable text.

pages.title: Everyone Wins the Race
pages.text: Alice and the wet animals climbed onto dry land. A Dodo suggested a race to dry them off. They ran any way they liked, stopping whenever they pleased. Who had won? Everyone! Alice shared little sweets as prizes. For her own prize, the Dodo gave her a thimble she already owned.
pages.scene: On the bank of the magical pool, Alice accepts a tiny thimble from a solemn Dodo while a Mouse, Duck and other damp animals gather around. Bright playful watercolor, little footprints in the mud, happy confusion, no readable text.
pages.sourceNote: Original narrative episode: Everyone Wins the Race.
pages.alt: On the bank of the magical pool, Alice accepts a tiny thimble from a solemn Dodo while a Mouse, Duck and other damp animals gather around. Bright playful watercolor, little footprints in the mud, happy confusion, no readable text.

pages.title: Too Big for the House
pages.text: The Rabbit mistook Alice for his servant and sent her to fetch his gloves. Inside his house, another drink made her grow until she filled the room. How could she get out? Small cakes appeared on the floor. One bite made her tiny again, and she hurried into the woods.
pages.scene: Outside a whimsical little cottage, an enormous Alice looks through an upstairs window with one arm resting out through it. The White Rabbit stands below, astonished, holding his watch. No damage, injury or duplicate versions of Alice; cheerful garden colors.
pages.sourceNote: Original narrative episode: Too Big for the House.
pages.alt: Portrait riverbank scene at the edge of Alice's tear‑pool. Present characters: Alice, White Rabbit, Mouse, Dodo (and other wet creatures implied). Composition: Alice sitting on a little heap of sticks, wet animals swimming and scrambling up the bank; the White Rabbit peering anxiously; watercolor splash of droplets and muddied feathers.

pages.title: Advice from a Caterpillar
pages.text: On a mushroom sat a blue Caterpillar. “Who are you?” he asked. Alice hardly knew after changing size so often. He told her that opposite sides of the mushroom would make her grow or shrink. With careful little bites, she learned to choose her size. At last, she had some control.
pages.scene: Alice stands beside a broad mushroom, talking to a large blue Caterpillar curled comfortably on top. Small mushroom pieces rest in her hands. Soft green woodland light, thoughtful expressions, gentle original watercolor; no smoking equipment or lettering.
pages.sourceNote: Original narrative episode: Advice from a Caterpillar.
pages.alt: Portrait exterior and cottage interior hint. Present characters: Alice, White Rabbit, Puppy. Composition: Split composition: foreground shows Alice tiny, peering after the Rabbit's house with a cake in hand; background vignette shows a moment of her towering inside a window. Puppy in mid‑leap, watercolor motion blur.

pages.title: A Baby, a Pig, a Grin
pages.text: Alice found a noisy kitchen full of pepper. The Duchess handed her a baby, but outside it turned into a pig and trotted away! Then a smiling cat appeared in a tree. It pointed her toward the March Hare. Slowly, the cat vanished—until only its grin was left.
pages.scene: In a green woodland clearing, Alice watches a small pig trot safely away while the striped Cheshire Cat smiles from a branch above. Its tail is fading into the leaves. Playful surprise, warm watercolor light, a single coherent scene without the kitchen.
pages.sourceNote: Original narrative episode: A Baby, a Pig, a Grin.
pages.alt: In a green woodland clearing, Alice watches a small pig trot safely away while the striped Cheshire Cat smiles from a branch above. Its tail is fading into the leaves. Playful surprise, warm watercolor light, a single coherent scene without the kitchen.

pages.title: Tea That Never Ends
pages.text: The Hatter, March Hare and sleepy Dormouse sat at a crowded tea table. Their clock seemed stuck at teatime. They asked riddles, argued and kept changing seats. Alice finally had enough. She left, found a door in a tree, and returned to the hall. This time, she reached the garden.
pages.scene: Alice sits at a long garden tea table with the Hatter, March Hare and sleepy Dormouse. Mismatched cups and a teapot crowd the table. The Hatter wears a plain tall hat without a label. Comic expressions, loose warm watercolor, no readable signs.
pages.sourceNote: Original narrative episode: Tea That Never Ends.
pages.alt: Portrait kitchen interior, warm and peppery. Present characters: Alice, Duchess, Cook, Baby (turning into a Pig), Cheshire Cat. Composition: Alice holding the piglet‑baby in the foreground, the Duchess bustling, white pepper clouds from the cook, Cheshire Cat grinning above on a mantel, watercolor steam and bright hearth glow.

pages.title: The Queen’s Strange Game
pages.text: Gardeners shaped like playing cards were painting white roses red. Then the Queen of Hearts arrived, shouting angry orders. She invited Alice to play croquet—but the balls were hedgehogs, and the mallets were flamingos! Nothing would stay still. Alice was beginning to see how foolish the Queen could be.
pages.scene: Alice gently holds a flamingo during a chaotic garden croquet game while a hedgehog walks away unharmed. The Queen of Hearts in a red heart-patterned gown gestures impatiently. Card-shaped gardeners and red roses behind them. Whimsical and non-violent, no readable text.
pages.sourceNote: Original narrative episode: The Queen’s Strange Game.
pages.alt: Portrait garden tea scene in muted morning light. Present characters: Alice, Hatter, March Hare, Dormouse. Composition: Low table crowded with teacups and cake; Hatter tipping a hat and March Hare mid‑spill, Dormouse half asleep; Alice standing to leave, watercolor tea steam curling upward; distant tree with hidden door visible.

pages.title: The Mock Turtle’s Story
pages.text: A creature called the Gryphon led Alice to the sad Mock Turtle. He told her about his school beneath the sea, where every lesson had a very odd name. Alice listened and asked questions. Nothing in Wonderland worked quite like home—not even a school day.
pages.scene: Alice sits beside the melancholy Mock Turtle on a seaside rock while the Gryphon listens. The Mock Turtle has a turtle shell, a gentle calf-like head and small hooves. The Gryphon has an eagle head and wings with a lion body. Soft blue-green watercolor shore.
pages.sourceNote: Original narrative episode: The Mock Turtle’s Story.
pages.alt: Portrait garden at noon. Present characters: Alice, Queen of Hearts, Cheshire Cat, Gardeners. Composition: Alice in mid‑swing with a flamingo, gardeners bent over a rosebush painting petals red, the Queen striding forward pointing, Cheshire Cat grinning from a tree limb above; watercolor splashes of red and green.

pages.title: A Very Silly Dance
pages.text: The Mock Turtle and Gryphon showed Alice a dance called the Lobster Quadrille. They sang, turned and skipped as they described lobsters dancing in the sea. Alice tried to tell them about her own adventures. Then a shout interrupted everything: the trial was beginning! The Gryphon hurried her away.
pages.scene: The Mock Turtle and Gryphon demonstrate a funny dance on a sandy shore while Alice watches with delight. Their poses are playful and balanced, the sea sparkling behind them. Original watercolor creatures matching the prior scene; no captions or musical lettering.
pages.sourceNote: Original narrative episode: A Very Silly Dance.
pages.alt: Portrait shoreline rock and shallow sea impression. Present characters: Alice, Gryphon, Mock Turtle. Composition: Mock Turtle sitting on a low rock, cap askew, sing‑leading, Gryphon bowing or prancing, Alice in the centre clapping; soft wash of blue‑green behind them, dancers implied in motion.

pages.title: Who Took the Tarts?
pages.text: In the courtroom, the Knave of Hearts was accused of stealing the Queen’s tarts. The Hatter and other witnesses gave answers that made little sense. Meanwhile, Alice began to grow again. The court seemed less frightening as she grew taller. Then the White Rabbit called her as the next witness.
pages.scene: Alice stands in a crowded storybook courtroom, growing taller than the small playing-card court. The White Rabbit holds a trumpet beside the King and Queen of Hearts. A plate of tarts rests on a table. Funny, confused expressions, no readable papers or labels.
pages.sourceNote: Original narrative episode: Who Took the Tarts?.

pages.title: Home from Wonderland
pages.text: Alice refused to accept the court’s silly rules. “You’re nothing but a pack of cards!” she cried. The cards flew up—and suddenly she woke beside her sister. It had all been a dream. Alice ran home for tea, while her sister smiled and imagined those wonderful adventures for herself.
pages.scene: Alice sits awake beside her older sister on a peaceful riverbank. A book lies closed in the grass, and a few ordinary leaves drift in the breeze. Alice smiles as she tells her dream. Gentle afternoon sunlight and warm watercolor, no magical characters or floating cards.
pages.sourceNote: Original narrative episode: Home from Wonderland.
pages.alt: Portrait riverbank late afternoon, gentle light. Present characters: Alice and Sister. Composition: Alice seated, hair mussed, wakeful and smiling in her sister's lap; grass and a tipped-up book beside them; watercolor ripples on the river and fallen cards faintly brushed away like leaves.
